candidate_diagrams.claim: The six basis vectors of V(2ω1) form two color-labeled lowering strings, with shared vertices v12 and v23, and these six arrows are exactly the crystal graph.
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The example gives all six vertices, explicit color-1/color-2 strings, and verifies there are no other arrows. A graph turns those shared-vertex incidence relations into a single inspectable object.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Draw vertices v11,v12,v22,v13,v23,v33 with color-1 arrows v11→v12→v22 and v13→v23, and color-2 arrows v12→v13 and v22→v23→v33. Label nodes by the displayed ω-weights; do not imply arrows carry the quantum coefficients [2], since these are crystal residue arrows.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, strongly source-supported; optional visualization of an explicit finite graph

candidate_diagrams.claim: The product basis cells (j,k) of an (a+1)×(b+1) rectangle are partitioned into residue strings: first move in the j direction until j=a−t, then move in the k direction, for each t≤min(a,b).
candidate_diagrams.kind: rank-one tensor crystal grid and string partition
candidate_diagrams.why_warranted: The statement gives piecewise operator rules and an explicit partition of a rectangular set into chains; the staircase boundary j=a−t organizes where each string switches tensor factors.
candidate_diagrams.specific_content: Show a small generalizable rectangle with cells (j,k), a few chains for successive t, arrows for lowering, and the switch at j=a−t; annotate that the branch condition is a−j>k versus a−j≤k. Mark it schematic and avoid suggesting the picture replaces the stated formulas for arbitrary a,b.
candidate_diagrams.confidence: possible, source-supported; optional aid for the explicit piecewise crystal map
